title: Regression pin's substring probe contradicts its own false-positive claim
evidence:
+  // `data-disabled-reason` must not false-positive.
+  let assert Ok(#(tag_tail, _)) = string.split_once(after, ">")
+  tag_tail
+  |> string.contains("disabled")
+  |> should.be_false
detail: The comment promises a `data-disabled-reason` attribute must not false-positive, but `string.contains(tag_tail, "disabled")` matches that substring verbatim. If such an attribute is ever added to the button, the pin fails spuriously — the claimed protection does not exist.
recommended_fix: Probe for `" disabled"` (leading space) or split the tail on whitespace and compare whole tokens, so only a bare `disabled` attribute fails the pin; otherwise soften the comment's claim.

title: JS-side consent gating now hinges on form.js init behavior asserted but not shown in this diff
evidence:
-            attribute("disabled", ""),
+- `server/priv/static/form.js` — gate coordination (`data-consent-blocked`, `data-preflight-blocked`, `__rtRecomputeSubmitDisabled`). Unchanged; its init `refresh()` is what disables the button when JS runs.
detail: Removing the SSR `disabled` is safe only if form.js unconditionally disables an initially-enabled button on init. That behavior is asserted in the spec but not evidenced in the diff; if recompute keys off the pre-existing attribute, JS gating breaks.
recommended_fix: Include the relevant form.js init/recompute excerpt in the review packet or quote it in the spec so reviewers can verify the gate disables the button regardless of its initial attribute state.
